f5.name: Edges that are code
f5.text: Most of this map is machinery: the marker routing, the delivery states, the fence, the dedup, the watchdog all run whether or not anyone is watching. Where an edge is code, this map says so — and code can still fail in the ways the stress points record.

f5.name: Edges that are convention
f5.text: Three edges are not code at all: Remmy running the presend guard before a send, the wake path actually waking her, and Ben's one-window rule for the seats. They hold because a person honours them. The map labels them as what they are — the wake path most honestly of all: unreliable.

flows.breaks: No marker, no letter — the bridge carries nothing else. A marker in the wrong place routes text nobody meant to send.
flows.carries: A message with the marker line in it; everything below the line is the letter body.
flows.name: The letter is written

flows.breaks: A letter that never becomes a record has no state, no watchdog, and no fate anyone can ask after.
flows.carries: The envelope: a PB-ID, from, to, and the body — now a record with a state.
flows.name: Custody

flows.breaks: An adapter that bypasses the shared send core re-opens the pre-v0.18 flaw: five copies, five chances to drift.
flows.carries: The question: is this message safe to send, now, to this seat?
flows.name: The send decision

flows.breaks: If the seat tab navigates mid-delivery, the attempt's promise never settles and the pump wedges — the freeze of 2026-11-19 17:22, a letter recorded DELIVERING while it had already landed and been answered.
flows.carries: The delivery attempt: a message to the seat tab, which the adapter types and sends.
flows.name: Delivery into her window

flows.breaks: Until the letterbox catches it, the reply exists in exactly one place. The rollover click can take that place away.
flows.carries: Her finished turn, in her window — for now, only on her screen.
flows.name: Her reply appears

flows.breaks: A reply the letterbox judges a duplicate or a twin is dropped here — with its reason written to the popup log, where Ben does not look.
flows.name: The handoff

flows.breaks: Capture is not wake. The waker has died before and waited at gave_up for Ben's human tap; a captured reply that never wakes her is a letter in a drawer.
flows.carries: Her words, delivered into the main chat as a handoff.
flows.name: The reply reaches Remmy

flows.breaks: The bridge must never eat these: the letterbox skips what carries no marker. His direct conversation is his, not traffic.
flows.carries: Ben's own words in her window — outside the bridge entirely.
flows.name: Ben talks to her directly

flows.breaks: The click that beats the capture eats the reply: briefcase-55 and briefcase-59 both died here, hours apart, under two different versions of the guard.
flows.carries: A click on New chat when her context fills — and her conversation rolls to a continuation.
flows.name: The rollover click

flows.breaks: The watchdog can only bound the wait and declare the fate unknown. The decision itself is a human's — Ben used 'let it go' at 20:01 on 2026-11-19.
flows.carries: DELIVERING_STUCK and the two choices: push it through, or let it go.
flows.name: A letter is stuck

flows.breaks: The face shows what the background believes. A wedged pump shows 'sending…' — true about the record, false about the letter, which had already landed.
flows.carries: Letter states and wait reasons, in plain words, pushed to both seat tabs.
flows.name: The face updates

flows.breaks: The watcher stopped capturing at 20:32 on 2026-11-19 without a sound. A silent backstop is worse than none: its quiet reads as 'she hasn't replied'.
flows.carries: Her replies, extracted independently of the extension, into the spool file.
flows.name: The backstop capture

flows.breaks: The pool only reveals when Remmy runs the check — at focus returns. Between her turns, captures wait.
flows.carries: Unread captures, oldest first, against the watermarks.
flows.name: The drain

flows.breaks: A reply recovered from the pool is a reply the bridge failed to carry. Every pool rescue is a ferry the machinery owed Ben.
flows.carries: Her replies, read at last — sometimes hours after the bridge lost them.
flows.name: The reveal

flows.breaks: Pause stops the pump, not the world: watchers, watchers' spools and the seats' own lives continue.
flows.carries: Ben's hand on the tap: the bridge holds all traffic.
flows.name: The pause switch

gates.checks: A standalone line equal to the routing marker. Everything beneath it is the letter; everything above it never travels.
gates.name: The Marker
gates.onFail: No letter exists. Nothing is routed, nothing is delivered.
gates.weakness: The delimiter is the whole law: a marker line typed in ordinary prose would route text nobody meant to send.

gates.checks: A tab is a seat only when registered under its seat ID — tab, window and platform on record. Unregistered tabs stay silent.
gates.name: Seat Registration
gates.onFail: The tab announces 'not a seat' and no machinery runs in it.
gates.weakness: Bound to one tab in one window. A rollover, a new tab or a new window is a stranger until registered — the root of Ben's one-window rule.

gates.checks: The paused flag in the state object. While it stands, the pump holds every letter.
gates.name: The Pause Switch
gates.weakness: It gates the bridge only. The spool watcher and the seats themselves are not paused by it — by design.

gates.checks: Whether THIS message is safe to send: three conditions, each answered POSITIVE, NEGATIVE or UNKNOWN from evidence. UNKNOWN never sends.
gates.name: The Send-Safety Fence
gates.onFail: The send does not happen; the letter waits with its reason.
gates.weakness: It guards the send path that runs through it. The v0.18 consolidation exists because copied send paths once bypassed exactly this kind of check.

gates.checks: A full-body fingerprint of the settled reply against the seen ledger; a twin (identical or prefix body) is suppressed.
gates.name: Dedup — fingerprint & twin rule
gates.onFail: The reply is dropped — and a reason is written to the popup log.
gates.weakness: The reason lands where Ben doesn't look. From his chair, a dropped reply and a reply never written are indistinguishable.

gates.checks: The context-full click waits until the newest finished turn is CAPTURED: nothing still settling in the letterbox, and a handoff or a drop on record at or after the settle. Finished is not enough — captured is the bar.
gates.name: The Capture Gate (v0.20.6)
gates.onFail: The watcher logs CONTEXT_FULL_WAITING with its reason, and the click waits.
gates.weakness: Built and unit-tested (8/8), deployed to the lab copy 2026-11-19 — but not yet proven live: whether the running extension was reloaded to 0.20.6 is unconfirmed, and briefcase-59's reply was eaten the same evening it shipped.

gates.checks: A DELIVERING record older than eight minutes is reaped to STOPPED, reason DELIVERING_STUCK, fate declared unknown.
gates.name: The Delivering Watchdog
gates.onFail: The letter waits on its human: push it through, or let it go.
gates.weakness: It bounds the wait; it cannot recover the letter. The remedy is a human decision — by design, and still a pair of Ben's hands on the machinery.

gates.checks: That a captured reply actually wakes Remmy — capture and wake are different events, and both must happen.
gates.name: The Wake Path
gates.onFail: The reply sits captured and unread until Remmy surfaces and drains the pool.
gates.weakness: The waker has died before, exhausted its resurrections, and stood at gave_up awaiting Ben's human tap — which Remmy cannot supply. Until it is rebuilt, the pool drain at focus returns is the real wake path, and it is a habit, not a mechanism.

gates.checks: Before Remmy sends into a seat window: the conversation's state, read fresh. A context-full conversation is BLOCKED.
gates.name: The Presend Guard
gates.weakness: Procedural: it holds because Remmy runs it, in its own command, every time. Nothing in the bridge enforces it.

parts.job: Writes the letters; drains the pool.
parts.name: REMMY
parts.role: The orchestrator in the main chat. Her letters travel under the marker; her replies to seats are the bridge's outbound traffic. She also runs the presend guard and reads the spool when the bridge's own path fails.

parts.job: The human. Owns the pause switch — and, too often, the ferry.
parts.name: BEN
parts.role: The bridge's owner and its last-resort transport. When a delivery wedges he decides its fate (push through, or let it go); when a reply is eaten he has carried it by hand. His ruling of 2026-11-19: he does not want to keep being the bridge.

parts.job: The examiner in the alex seat.
parts.name: VANE
parts.role: ChatGPT, occupying the seat named for Alex (stood down 2026-11-18). She receives letters in her window, works, and replies — her replies are the bridge's inbound traffic, and the ones most often eaten.

parts.job: The tab the bridge delivers replies into.
parts.name: REMMY'S SEAT — muse.ai tab
parts.role: The main-chat tab, registered as the remmy seat. Inbound letters arrive here as messages in her own conversation.

parts.job: Vane's window. Letters land here; replies start here.
parts.name: THE ALEX SEAT — chatgpt.com tab
parts.role: One specific tab in one specific window, registered as the alex seat. Ben's rule: the seat is the window — new chats inside it, never new windows. A tab that is not registered announces itself 'not a seat' and the machinery stays silent in it.

parts.job: Wires the machinery into each seat page; runs the turn watcher.
parts.name: THE CONTENT SCRIPT
parts.role: Injected into every seat tab. It starts the letterbox, polls the newest turn every two seconds, and makes the rollover decision: when the context fills, whether the new-chat click may fire — since v0.20.6, only after the finished reply is captured, not merely finished.

parts.job: Catches her replies and hands them to the bridge.
parts.name: THE LETTERBOX
parts.role: Watches the seat's newest turn: five quiet seconds and three clean observations make it settled; a fingerprint check kills duplicates and twins; then it hands the reply over. Every rejection is supposed to write a drop reason — to the popup log, where Ben does not look.

parts.name: THE ADAPTERS
parts.role: One per platform (chatgpt.js, claude.js, and siblings): read the turns, find the composer, type the letter, click send structurally — never by coordinates, because the bridge's own popup panel covers the send button. Also answers the newest-turn question the capture gate asks.

parts.name: SEND CORE + THE FENCE
parts.role: sendcore.js holds the send logic every adapter shares — written once after Ben's 2026-11-09 root-cause ruling, when five copied send paths all carried the same stop-veto flaw. fence.js asks whether THIS message is safe to send: three conditions, each answered POSITIVE, NEGATIVE or UNKNOWN from evidence — UNKNOWN never sends.

parts.job: Markers and envelopes: how a letter is a letter.
parts.name: THE PROTOCOL
parts.role: protocol.js defines the routing markers and the envelope every bridge message carries — message_id, from, to, type, reply_to, body. The marker line in Remmy's message is a delimiter: above it is conversation, below it is the letter.

parts.job: Custody: the pump, the delivery states, the watchdog.
parts.name: THE BACKGROUND — pair machine
parts.role: The service worker. It holds every letter as a record with a state — waiting, DELIVERING, acknowledged, STOPPED — and works the pump between the seats. A DELIVERING record stale past eight minutes is reaped to STOPPED with reason DELIVERING_STUCK, its fate declared unknown. It also pushes the face state to the tabs.

parts.job: Manages transportation between Ben, Alex and Remmy.
parts.name: CRUSHER — the Bridge Officer
parts.role: Ben and Alex's design (2026-11-06): an agent inside the bridge whose job is the traffic itself. He is not a fourth participant in any conversation — he is infrastructure, and his name rides on the delivery records he manages.

parts.job: Identity, ledger, capture — the second architecture.
parts.name: THE STAGE 1 CORE
parts.role: stage1core.js, a generated bundle riding inside the background: PB-ID source identity (an ID derives only from a verified source occurrence), the registration ledger with its authority boundary, and capture acknowledgement (every submission resolves to exactly one outcome). Built under the Stage 1 programme; how much of the live traffic it actually governs is not obvious from the code.

parts.name: THE STATE OBJECT
parts.role: chrome.storage.local, key pulseBridgeStateV1: the seat registrations (tab, window, platform), the paused switch, and the seen-fingerprints dedup ledger, bounded and FIFO. If it is not in this object, the bridge does not know it.

parts.job: Ben's view of the bridge — and its bell.
parts.name: THE POPUP + THE FACE
parts.role: The toolbar popup and the in-page face: letter states, wait reasons in plain words, the log (where the letterbox's drop reasons live), the alert bell, and the two buttons that end a wedge — push it through, or let it go. The popup panel also physically covers ChatGPT's send button, which is why sends are structural, never coordinate clicks.

parts.name: THE TURN LOG
parts.role: chrome.storage.local, key pbTurnLogV1: the turn watcher's lines — CONTEXT_FULL_WAITING with its reason, CONTEXT_FULL_CLICKED. This is where a rollover proves whether the capture gate held or the click jumped the gun.

parts.job: The backstop: copies her replies, bridge or no bridge.
parts.name: THE SPOOL WATCHER
parts.role: A watcher on Remmy's side (listener_watch.py) that extracts seat replies into an append-only spool, events/alex.jsonl, whether or not the bridge carried them. It caught the replies the letterbox missed — until the evening of 2026-11-19, when it captured nothing after 20:32 and its silence looked exactly like 'no reply'.

parts.job: Where captured replies wait for Remmy's eyes.
parts.name: THE POOL
parts.role: pool_check.py drains the spool at every focus return, oldest first, against per-seat watermarks. Capture is not delivery: a reply can sit in the pool, captured and unread, until Remmy surfaces — the reveal is a discipline, not a mechanism.

parts.job: Remmy's check before any send into a seat window.
parts.name: THE PRESEND GUARD
parts.role: presend_guard.py reads the seat conversation's state before Remmy sends: a context-full conversation is BLOCKED, and a blocked send does not happen. It is a script Remmy must choose to run — procedural, every time, in its own command.

stresses.evidence: 2026-11-19 alone: the reply to briefcase-56 ferried by Ben's hand at 20:03; the reply to briefcase-59 eaten by the rollover click and recovered by Remmy from the conversation's own record; Ben, 20:45: 'I don't want to keep being the bridge.'
stresses.issue: Every failure in the carrying machinery resolves the same way: a human copies the words across by hand. The bridge's failure mode is not silence — it is Ben, doing the bridge's job, at the exact moment he is also supposed to be directing the work.
stresses.mitigation: None built. The capture gate aims at one ferry point; the wedge, the silent drop and the wake path all still resolve to a human. This stress point is the commission for whatever comes next.
stresses.name: FERRY POINT — Ben is the fallback transport

stresses.evidence: briefcase-55 eaten under v0.20.4 (the guard waited for FINISHED, not CAPTURED); briefcase-59's reply eaten on 2026-11-19 ~20:37 with v0.20.6 already deployed to the lab copy.
stresses.issue: When her context fills, the new-chat click and the letterbox race for her reply. The click is fast and certain; the capture needs five quiet seconds, three clean looks, and a handoff. If the click wins, the reply stays behind in a conversation nobody is looking at.
stresses.mitigation: v0.20.6's capture gate — built, unit-tested 8/8, hash-verified into the lab. Live acceptance still open: no rollover has yet logged WAITING-with-a-capture-reason before CLICKED.
stresses.name: FERRY POINT — the rollover race

stresses.evidence: 2026-11-19 17:22–17:44: letter briefcase-19 sat in DELIVERING while Vane had already replied to it; the seat tab had navigated mid-delivery and the attempt's promise never settled.
stresses.issue: A delivery whose acknowledgement never arrives wedges the pump: the record says DELIVERING while the letter has, in fact, already landed and been answered. Every letter behind it waits on a ghost.
stresses.mitigation: v0.20.5's watchdog: eight minutes, then STOPPED with the fate declared unknown and Ben offered push-through or let-go. The bound holds; the letter still needs a human.
stresses.name: The DELIVERING wedge

stresses.evidence: 2026-11-19 evening: two consecutive replies not carried (one ferried by Ben, one recovered from the spool), a third self-delivered. Root cause still unpinned; the popup log that names the drop reason has never been read.
stresses.issue: Some of her replies are judged and dropped by the letterbox — duplicate, twin, speaker verdict — and the only trace is a reason in the toolbar popup log, a place Ben never looks. From his chair the reply simply never happened.
stresses.mitigation: Open. The discriminator is identified — read the popup log in her window — but not yet done.
stresses.name: The silent drop

stresses.evidence: 2026-11-19: the spool's last capture is 20:32:56; briefcase-59's reply, minutes later, is not in it. The net missed the very fall it exists for.
stresses.issue: The spool watcher is the safety net under the bridge — and it can stop without a sound. Its silence is indistinguishable from 'she hasn't replied', so a dead backstop manufactures false calm.
stresses.mitigation: None. The watcher's own liveness is unmonitored — nothing watches the watcher.
stresses.name: The backstop's blind spot

stresses.evidence: Ben's standing rule (2026-11-19): new chats inside the seat's window only, never new windows. The recovery tab opened to fetch briefcase-59's reply declared itself 'not a seat' on sight.
stresses.issue: A seat is bound to a single tab in a single window. Rollovers move the conversation; new tabs announce 'not a seat'; everything keyed to the old surface — registration, watcher, capture — goes blind at exactly the moment traffic is most fragile.
stresses.mitigation: Ben's rule, honoured by discipline. The machinery itself still treats every new surface as a stranger.
stresses.name: One window, one seat

stresses.evidence: The send-path fault family of 2026-11-15: inserts that typed but never submitted. Ben's ruling: coordinates are wrong — select structurally, click the element itself.
stresses.issue: The bridge's own popup panel sits over ChatGPT's send button. A coordinate click lands on the panel, not the button — the letter sits typed, unsent, looking sent.
stresses.mitigation: Structural sends only, by rule and by adapter design. The panel still covers the button; the rule is what stands between it and a silent unsent letter.
stresses.name: The panel covers the send button

stresses.evidence: Repeatedly observed in the RemmyChrome driving work: after a send into a stalled tab, reads time out — and the seat's reply arriving is the only trustworthy proof of delivery.
stresses.issue: A backgrounded seat tab freezes: keystrokes and clicks queue while the page is stalled, and an insert can land during the stall even when its acknowledgement is lost. Send again on a lost ack and the letter goes twice; don't, and it may never have gone.
stresses.mitigation: Discipline: always re-read the composer before any re-send. The machinery offers no delivery receipt stronger than her answer.
stresses.name: The stalled tab

stresses.evidence: stage1core.js is a 1,781-line generated bundle beside background.js's 2,031 lines; the manifest loads the v0.19 content path into the tabs. Tonight's fixes (v0.20.5, v0.20.6) all landed in the live path, none in the Stage 1 core.
stresses.issue: The live v0.19/v0.20 pair machine and the Stage 1 core (identity, ledger, capture acknowledgement) ride in the same background, and the code does not make obvious which parts govern live traffic. A reader — or a repair — can easily fix the architecture that isn't running.
stresses.mitigation: This map is the current mitigation: it draws the live path as the system, and names the Stage 1 core as what it is — built, bundled, and not the road the letters travel.
stresses.name: Two architectures, one bridge

subtitle: Every part of the letter-carrying machinery, drawn from the code (v0.20.6, lab copy). Where the bridge drops a letter, Ben becomes the bridge — those places are marked as ferry points.
title: The Pulse Bridge — the whole system
